# StreamDek Mobile v2.1.17

*Version code 75*

## What's New

**Trailers in the quality you want**
Trailers now play at the resolution set in **Settings → Trailer quality**, up to 4K where the
trailer offers it. Until now nearly every trailer arrived at 360p whatever that setting said. 
StreamDek now asks in a way that gets the whole file, so a two-minute trailer at 1080p — around 
50 MB — plays in full rather than being ruled out before it starts.

**Trailers play to the end**
A trailer that stopped part way through, or cut out mid-scene and dropped back to the artwork, was
running out of the portion StreamDek was allowed to fetch. That limit no longer applies, and
trailers run to their last frame.

**Trailers in the film's own language**
Studios upload a trailer with its dubbed versions attached — eight languages is ordinary — and
StreamDek could pick any one of them, because it chose the version encoded at the highest quality
rather than the one the film was made in. On one trailer the German dub was a fraction ahead of the
English original, so the English film played in German. StreamDek now uses the original language
track that the upload itself identifies.

**More trailer links simply work**
Trailers arrive from catalogues and add-ons in whatever form each one uses. Short links, embedded
players, Shorts, premiere and live pages, privacy-mode links and plain video ids are now all
understood. Links StreamDek could not read before were treated as "no trailer at all", even when
the video behind them was fine.

**Streaming network pages keep loading**
Browsing a streaming network's titles now loads the next page as you reach the bottom, and keeps
loading while there is more to show. Titles that appear on more than one page are shown once.
Searching within a network pages the same way, and clearing the search returns you to the network's
titles where you left them.

**Play, Resume and Play again say the right thing**
A film's main button now follows where you actually are in it. Starting a film you have watched
before shows **Resume** while you are part way through, rather than still offering **Play again**
from an earlier viewing, and returns to **Play again** once you reach the end. Marking a film
unwatched returns it to **Play**.

**Navigation that moves out of the way while you scroll**
**Settings → Appearance and Language → Navigation Behaviour** now offers three choices:
**Expanded**, **Collapse After a Delay** — the collapsible navigation you already had — and the new
**Collapse While Scrolling**. With the new option, the navigation tucks into your profile button as
soon as you move through a page, in either direction, and stays tucked away through a fling or a
run of quick swipes. When you stop, it comes back about half a second later. A finger resting on
the screen counts as still browsing, and tapping the profile button brings the navigation back
straight away.

**Search that makes room for results**
On Search, a streaming network's page, **View all** lists and live channel lists, the header now
condenses as you scroll down: the title, filters and channel chips fold away and only the search box
stays, pinned to the top. With the Modern header style, the glass panel closes into a floating pill
around the search box. Scroll back up and the header rebuilds itself piece by piece. Search stays
fully open while you are typing, even as you scroll through results with the keyboard up.

The search box is now the same on every one of these pages — the same shape, colour, width and
place on the screen, with no outline — and the poster grid beneath it sits at the same margins as
Search's everywhere, so a title looks the same size however you reached it.

**Continue Watching and Watchlist keep their controls**
The headers on Continue Watching and your Watchlist condense the same way, but keep their top row:
the page name, the number of titles, **Clear all** and the grid size stay within reach while the
filter chips fold away.

**Visual Effects**
A new **Visual Effects** setting under **Appearance** balances StreamDek's glass against smooth
scrolling. **Automatic** is the default and picks the richest look your phone can keep smooth.
**Full** always uses glass blur where Android supports it, and **Reduced** keeps the translucent
look with tinted glass instead of live blur. When Automatic is using the lighter look, the setting
says why — Battery Saver, the phone itself, or scrolling that had slowed down. Saved on this device
only.

**Glass that stays readable**
Headers and the navigation now add a little shading behind their icons and text when a bright
title image or busy posters sit underneath, instead of looking the same over everything. The status
bar gets the same care: on Home, Search, Continue Watching, your Watchlist and title pages, a soft
shade fades in behind the clock and battery once content scrolls beneath them, and fades away again
at the top of the page.

## Improvements

- **The right trailer, chosen more often.** StreamDek now reads what the catalogue says each video
  is — trailer, teaser, clip, featurette, whether the studio published it and when — instead of
  working it out afterwards by fetching each one. In the weeks around a release, when a title's
  videos are mostly ticket adverts and "Now Playing" stings, the actual trailer is picked out
  before anything is downloaded. For a series, the show's own trailer is preferred to a single
  season's teaser.
- **Trailers recover instead of failing.** Trailer links are issued against one of several servers,
  and a server that refuses meant no trailer at all. StreamDek now checks the link works before
  playing and moves to another server when it does not.
- **A trailer that cannot be found stays out of the way.** When no trailer can be played, the
  details page carries on exactly as it is, with the artwork in place. Nothing about the failure is
  put in front of you.
- **Trailers stay inside StreamDek.** Nothing about trailer playback opens a browser or another app.
- **Smoother on older and lower-powered phones.** Phones with less memory, phones running Android 11
  or earlier, and any phone with Battery Saver on now use the lighter glass automatically, and the
  blurred backgrounds behind Home and title pages are drawn in a way that costs a fraction of the
  work.
- **Respects your accessibility settings.** With Android's animations turned off, headers and the
  navigation change without moving. With High Contrast Text on, glass surfaces lean on stronger
  shading behind their text.
- **A smoother start.** Choosing a profile no longer freezes the screen for a moment while your
  profile's sources load; that work now happens in the background. The profile picker, the
  **Preparing Home** screen and Home fade into one another instead of cutting, Home is built out of
  sight and revealed once its rows have arrived, and the navigation eases in as it appears.
- **The Default header style follows along.** Headers in the Default style now condense the same
  way: on Search, streaming network pages and **View all** lists the background goes away and the
  search box stays on a pill of its own, while Continue Watching and your Watchlist keep their title
  row on a band. At rest the Default header is lightly see-through, letting a little of the page
  show behind it.

## Fixed

- Fixed trailers playing at 360p regardless of the trailer quality setting.
- Fixed trailers stopping part way through and returning to the artwork.
- Fixed a trailer occasionally playing in a dubbed language rather than the film's own.
- Fixed trailer links in Shorts, premiere, live and privacy-mode forms being treated as though the
  title had no trailer.
- Fixed a trailer failing to start when the server its link was issued against would not answer.
- Fixed streaming network pages stopping after the first page of titles, and the same title
  appearing more than once while scrolling.
- Fixed a film you were part way through offering **Play again** instead of **Resume**.
- Fixed Home's loading placeholder not matching Home: it now shows the full-width spotlight with its
  title, button and page dots, and rows of cards at the size Home draws them, so the page fills in
  where it loads rather than rearranging.
- Fixed a square highlight flashing behind the round header buttons on Search, Continue Watching,
  your Watchlist, streaming network pages and **View all** lists.
- Fixed the blurred background behind Home and title pages appearing sharp on Android 11 and
  earlier.
- Fixed the navigation and Modern headers being hard to read on phones that cannot blur, where
  their glass was too faint to separate icons and text from the page behind.
- Fixed the search box on a **View all** list appearing only after you had scrolled far enough to
  load more titles, which shifted the page under your thumb.
- Fixed a hard line under the status bar on Search, streaming network pages and **View all** lists
  with the Default header style.
